subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 29, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - October 29, 2026

Hello AcreetionOS community,

We hope this newsletter finds you well. As we continue to push forward with our mission to create a community-driven, user-friendly Linux distribution based on Arch Linux, we wanted to take a moment to highlight some recent developments and updates.

Firstly, we'd like to share with you a report from the Linux Plumbers Conference (LPC) sched_ext microconference. The report highlights the discussions and insights gained from the conference, which is a great resource for anyone interested in the latest developments in the Linux community.

In other news, the Redox OS ring buffers project has made significant progress, and we encourage you to check out their project summary for more information.

On the security front, we've issued updates for AlmaLinux, Debian, and other distributions. These updates address various vulnerabilities and are essential for ensuring the security of your system.

In our own project, we've made several commits to our codebase, including updates to our intelligence sync, wiki guides, and feed. We're constantly working to improve and refine our distribution, and these changes will help us better serve our community.

We've also made some updates to our AcreetionOS-Xlibre repository, which is a key component of our distribution. These changes will help improve the overall user experience and ensure that our distribution remains stable and secure.

In addition to these updates, we've made some changes to our CI/CD infrastructure, including passing the -R flag to the gh release create command and fixing a block-scalar indentation issue in our release.yml file. These changes will help us streamline our release process and ensure that our distribution is always up-to-date.

We're also excited to announce that we've re-triggered our GitLab mirror, which will help us keep our codebase in sync and ensure that our community has access to the latest updates.

As always, we're grateful for your continued support and enthusiasm for the AcreetionOS project. We're committed to creating a distribution that is both user-friendly and secure, and we're excited to see where this journey takes us.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community, and we look forward to sharing more updates with you in the future.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift
